```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(bsu.tools)
library(ggplot2)
```

`bsu.tools` provides a ggplot2 theme and discrete scales that use UC Davis
Health styling. Add them to a plot with `+`, just like other ggplot2 components.

## Style points with color

Use `scale_color_ucdh()` when a discrete variable is mapped to the `color`
aesthetic. `theme_ucdh()` styles the plot text, grid, legend, and facet strips.

```{r color}
ggplot(
  iris,
  aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, color = Species)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Iris petal and sepal lengths",
    x = "Sepal length",
    y = "Petal length"
  ) +
  scale_color_ucdh() +
  theme_ucdh()
```

## Style areas with fill

Use `scale_fill_ucdh()` for discrete `fill` mappings, such as groups in a bar
chart.

```{r fill}
ggplot(
  mtcars,
  aes(factor(cyl), fill = factor(am))
) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Transmission by cylinder count",
    x = "Cylinders",
    y = "Cars"
  ) +
  scale_fill_ucdh(
    name = "Transmission",
    labels = c("Automatic", "Manual")
  ) +
  theme_ucdh()
```

## Customize the theme

The `base_size` and `base_family` arguments control the text, while
`grid_lines = FALSE` removes the panel grid. For example:

```{r customize}
ggplot(
  iris,
  aes(Sepal.Length, Petal.Length, color = Species)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_ucdh() +
  theme_ucdh(base_size = 13, grid_lines = FALSE)
```
